sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Senales, called Schnals by the municipality, is a valley municipality in South Tyrol of 1,229 inhabitants [17] whose parking question is about reaching the Kurzras glacier ski area and, increasingly, the villages along the road. The municipal council took basic decisions on car-park management in Kurzras and a convention with the Schnalstaler Gletscherbahnen AG in May 2023 and again in November 2024, approving a convention that delimits the areas; the register publishes only titles, so we do not know the content [0][1]. On 29 April 2026 the council decided to introduce paid parking zones in Vernagt, with the tariffs, zones and start date unknown [7]. On 20 December 2023 it set the contribution due in lieu of providing parking spaces for new buildings and extensions, without the amount being visible [12]. The road to Kurzras is asphalted and open all year, and the operator says bus line 261 runs hourly to Kurzras [14]. A provincial notice of December 2022 announced more trips on line 261 between Naturns and the valley but the cancellation of direct services to Meran, with a change in Naturns, so the current routing is unconfirmed [15].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The executive has been working on Vernagt and Karthaus. It contracted a temporary car park at Vernagt in 2024 and 2025 and approved the conditions for another for 2026 on 13 May 2026 [9]. The layout works of a permanent Vernagt car park with a connecting pavement were closed out in 2025, with the final state approved on 23 April 2025, and a contract for road markings and signage followed on 29 October 2025 [10]. In Karthaus, the municipal seat, it commissioned a variant study on the parking situation in October 2024 and a feasibility study for a car park in December 2024, and we found no decision to build [11]. It granted a contribution to the tourism cooperative for the ski bus in June 2025 and commissioned bus-stop works in Kurzras and Vernagt [13]. At Kurzras the glacier railway company finished a new valley station on 23 December 2024 with an underground garage; a diary entry gave 44 spaces, while the operator's parking page says about 40 [6].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The operator's page lists two car parks at Kurzras. The outdoor one, about 100 metres from the valley station, has no gate and records the number plate: 60 minutes free until 17:00, then 6 euros for the day and 12 euros for each further day, nothing to pay from 17:00 to 24:00 and 80 euros a day if unpaid [2]. It is run by Mobility Hub Parkservice Italia, and payment is by machine, by QR code or website within 24 hours, or through EasyPark [3]. The indoor car park has about 40 spaces at 1.50 euros an hour with a daily maximum of 18 euros [4]; a news item of March 2025 quoted 2.50 euros an hour and 24 euros, so the tariff has apparently been lowered [5]. On 6 May 2026 the executive approved agreements with EasyPark and Nexi for paying the municipality's parking fees [8]. The Caravan Park Schnals is a barrier-controlled motorhome site, open 24 hours, charging 36 to 46 euros a day per vehicle from June 2026 to May 2027; its own pages say 40 pitches in one place and 80 in another [16].

Our data cover two car parks. We could not match 'P4 Senales', with 42 spaces in the feed, to any source we read. It was measured for 24 days since 27 September 2026 and averaged about 23% on weekdays and 16% at weekends, with a peak of 60% on a Tuesday morning. The caravan park, with 120 spaces in the feed, averaged about 17% both on weekdays and weekends, from far fewer readings. These are autumn figures, outside the ski season.
